There are two kinds of chokes, trachea and blood chokes.

For trachea chokes the goal is simple, to close the trachea. I like to do a variant of the common guillotine choke that hits the trachea and then I like to use a trach based paper cutter to get them to turn under my elbow so I can find an opening to advance something. Trachea chokes are a lot more painful and panic inducing than blood chokes and don't tend to result in losing consciousness as quickly if at all. Usually people tap out from the pain of it and not the lack of air, it hurts very much to have your trachea forcibly closed.

The other kind of choke is a blood choke where you close the arteries on the side of the neck under the ears. This can result in loss of consciousness in like 5 seconds flat because the brain is deprived of oxygen and blood. Common blood chokes include the rear naked choke, the triangle choke, the north/south choke, the arm triangle, the anaconda and the darce choke. You can close off the arteries using your arms, your fist, their shoulder, your clothing or their clothing on either side and the result will be the same.

If you were to look up how to do any of these chokes you might think it is very simple to do. However, if you were to try to get them on an opponent that is fighting back you'd find out it is incredibly difficult to actually land any of these chokes and have it work properly against a resisting opponent. Even when you get them like it looks like on TV it often doesn't choke the other person at all and there are a million little details you have to get right.

A knee to the back of the neck is ABSOLUTELY NOT a way to choke someone to death and wouldn't result in asphyxia because it blocks neither blood nor oxygen. You don't come in contact with the trachea at all as it is on the complete other side, you don't come into contact with the arteries (1 even if you got them sideways is the most) and you aren't on the lungs at all.
